I started using a smart lock on my front door about five or six years ago, and I've tried quite a few models in that time. For most users, the ULTRALOQ Bolt Fingerprint is a solid choice — it supports Apple Home, has built-in Wi-Fi, and offers a comprehensive set of unlock methods. Whether you prefer using your fingerprint or simply a PIN code, it basically has you covered.

HomeKit Weekly is a column dedicated to smart home accessories, automation tips, and everything related to Apple's smart home framework.

Apple Home support, but no Home Key

ULTRALOQ positions the Bolt Fingerprint as its first smart lock with full Apple Home integration, and it's precisely this integration that drew me in. Honestly, I still miss Touch ID on the iPhone to this day. You can lock or unlock through the Home app or Siri, and if you have a HomePod or Apple TV acting as a home hub, the experience is just like any other Apple Home accessory — you can add it to automation scenes, control it remotely, and it's fully compatible with all kinds of scenes and automation routines.

However, for me, there's always been one missing feature: Home Key. Being able to simply tap your iPhone or Apple Watch to open the door — that's what truly feels like an upgrade. Although it's the only thing missing, it's not exactly a deal-breaker.

I hope ULTRALOQ will consider adding this feature in their next model, because with Home Key, this lock could go from being 'good' to being 'near perfect.' At the same time, the lock also supports Amazon Alexa, Google Home, SmartThings, and IFTTT — so no matter which smart home platform you prefer, or even if you plan to switch platforms down the road, it offers excellent flexibility. It uses 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi rather than Bluetooth, meaning you can perform basic remote control through its app without needing an additional bridge.

Plenty of unlock options

The Bolt Fingerprint offers a wide variety of unlock methods. The fingerprint reader can store up to 50 fingerprints and 50 codes, and you can unlock it via the mobile app, have it unlock automatically as you approach the door, or use voice control through Siri, Alexa, or Google Assistant. It also comes with two physical keys, so even if the battery dies, you won't be completely locked out. For me, a smart lock without a physical key as a backup is completely unacceptable.

You can also set up to 50 custom codes, and issue one-time or time-limited codes to friends, visitors, or cleaning staff. If you have a rental property, this feature alone is well worth the price of admission.

There's also a 'Lockout Mode' that temporarily disables all electronic unlock methods, including codes and app unlocking, giving people who are away for extended periods an extra layer of peace of mind and security when they're not home. Personally, I don't see these features as essential for a smart lock, but having them doesn't hurt either.

Installation and adding to Apple Home

I've installed more smart locks over the past few years than I can count, so I have quite a bit of experience by now. As long as I have the right tools, I can usually get it done in about ten minutes. Assuming you're replacing an existing modern deadbolt, the installation process doesn't require any wiring or drilling into walls. A Phillips screwdriver is all you need, and remember to replace the strike plate on the door frame at the same time.

After adding the lock to your Apple Home setup and assigning it to a room, you can control it through the Home app or include it in automations and scenes — triggering multiple actions at once, such as turning on the lights the moment the front door is unlocked.

ULTRALOQ Bolt Fingerprint overall review

Overall, if you don't need Home Key support, the ULTRALOQ Bolt Fingerprint is a reliable choice. Fingerprint unlocking will most likely become your everyday go-to method. The installation process is also very straightforward. I'm currently using this lock on my office door, because there are always laptops sitting around waiting to be shipped out, and I want that extra layer of security. The auto-unlock feature when you approach the door is genuinely excellent, and you can see at any time who's come and gone. The fingerprint unlock gives me the same feeling as using Touch ID back in the day.

You can buy the Bolt Fingerprint directly from Amazon or the ULTRALOQ official website.
